title: Grandad's bicycle
summary: A teenager repairs his grandfather's old bike and discovers a new way to see his town.
paragraphs: In his grandfather's garage, under a dusty blanket, Mateo found an old bicycle. It was heavy and black, with a leather seat and a bell that still worked. The {{tyres}} were flat, the chain was {{rusty}} and one of the brakes was missing. "That bike took me to work for thirty years," his grandfather said. "It's finished now."

Mateo wasn't so sure. He had never repaired anything bigger than a pen, but he watched videos online and made a list of the parts he needed. On Saturdays he went to a small bike shop where the owner, a woman called Sole, let him use her tools if he swept the floor. She taught him how to take the chain off, clean it and put it back.

It took two months. He bought new tyres with his birthday money, found a second-hand brake at a market and painted the frame. His grandfather came to the garage often. At first he just watched. Then he started giving advice, telling stories and, one day, holding the {{wheel}} while Mateo tightened it. They talked more in those two months than they had in years.

When the bike was finished, Mateo rode it to school. It was slow and heavy compared to his friends' bikes, and everybody laughed at the bell. But he noticed things he had never seen from the bus: a bakery that opened at six, a garden with a fig tree, an old man who fed the pigeons every morning in the same square.

One Sunday, he asked his grandfather to show him his old {{route}} to work. They went together, slowly, Mateo on the old bike and his grandfather on a new electric one that his family had given him. His grandfather pointed at buildings and told him what they used to be: a cinema, a school, a factory. "The town has changed," he said, "but the hills are just as steep." Mateo laughed. That was the one thing the electric bike had made easier.

rusty.meaning: covered in a red-brown layer that appears on old metal

wheel.meaning: a round object that turns and helps a vehicle move

route.meaning: the way you go from one place to another

tyres.meaning: the rubber rings around the wheels of a bike or car

questions.question: What did Mateo's grandfather think of the old bike?
options: He wanted Mateo to throw it away.

options: He swept the floor of the shop.
He worked in the shop every day.

questions.question: How did the project change Mateo and his grandfather?
options: They talked much more than before.
questions.explanation: They talked more in those two months than they had in years.

questions.question: Why did Mateo laugh at the end?
options: His grandfather fell off the bike.
The electric bike made the steep hills easier for his grandfather.
